title: [master] thermalctld leak on Arista devices makes them unreachable when memory is exhausted
author: Staphylo
body:

#### Description

On Arista devices `thermalctld` leaks memory (unclear if other vendors are affected).
At each loop iteration of `thermalctld` a few more MB are consumed (~3MiB every 60s)
After running for a few hours, `pmon` consumes up to 75% of memory at which point the device becomes unresponsive.
- Existing ssh sessions will freeze
- Console becomes unresponsive
- Pings still go through

#### Steps to reproduce the issue:
1. Install latest master image
2. Wait for a few hours while monitoring (you can make this faster by filling a tmpfs to reduce available memory)
    Run `docker stats` to see memory size of pmon growing
    Run `watch -d -n 1 'docker exec -ti pmon sh -c "ps aux | grep -v aux"'` to see memory growing at pmon process level
3. Witness ssh/console hanging while ping still working
4. After some more time kernel will panic

#### Output seen on the console after kernel panic

This issue is happening consistently on master.
It is currently being looked at and this issue opened for awareness.

comments.author: zzhiyuan
comments.body:
On an Arista device I can run the following snippet python code:

```
import sonic_platform
chassis = sonic_platform.platform.Platform().get_chassis()
while True:
   for sfp in chassis.get_all_sfps():
      sfp._get_sfputil().get_transceiver_dom_info_dict(sfp._index)
```

and it will result in a memory leak. I believe it is caused by:

https://github.com/Azure/sonic-platform-common/blob/master/sonic_platform_base/sonic_sfp/sfputilbase.py

There are many methods which opens a file without using the with statement. It is possible there are stray references to the opened file which results in memory leaks.

comments.author: zzhiyuan
comments.body: In master image on sonic-buildimage, most of the leak currently is from xcvrd, caused by the same issue referenced above. This is also applicable to 202012 image and likely other vendors' products. Andy from the Arista team is making the fix. This will also benefit other vendors.

comments.author: andywongarista
comments.body: The root cause of this issue has been determined to be in Arista platform drivers rather than in sfputilbase.py. A PR to update the submodule with the fix included will be made shortly.
